npcs.name: Maren Holt
npcs.motivation: Wants the mill running again to pay off her late mother's debt before the bailiff comes.

npcs.name: Tobiah Reed
npcs.motivation: Wants the mill to fail so the bailiff will sell it cheaply to him.

npcs.name: Wick
npcs.motivation: Wants his unpaid wages and a safe road out of the valley.

secrets.text: The sluice pin was filed through from the inside by Tobiah Reed, so that the wheel would jam and the mill would stop.
Wick is owed three months of pay by Tobiah and will switch sides if he hears that Tobiah never meant to pay him.
The shrine's keeper is long dead. Maren leaves the bread there in her father's memory.
Aldous hid in the cellar himself. Tobiah did not take him, and he is bound by his own hand to protect his daughter from a charge of theft.

sceneConditions.condition: If the party arrives after dark, Maren is absent and Scene 2 begins with the gate already open.
If the party makes noise in the yard, Wick arrives and the Scene 3 encounter begins on alert.
Once the lever is pulled, the cellar starts to flood and the party has about five turns.
If the party stays more than five turns, the water reaches the ceiling.

branch.description: A side path to a reed shrine that grants a re-roll and a hint, and can be skipped without blocking the ending.

alternativeSolution.description: Persuade Wick to stand aside by naming Tobiah's debt or showing the filed pin, instead of fighting him.

missableClue.clue: The sluice pin was sabotaged: a lock was fitted to it the week before the miller vanished.

endings.description: Tobiah is exposed, the bailiff cannot sell the mill, and the wheel turns again.
The cellar floods, Tobiah buys the mill, and Maren leaves the bend.

actionableDetails.detail: The party sees a rotting jetty, a silent stone mill with its wheel hanging still, and a woman waiting with folded arms.
Maren Holt meets the party at the jetty and asks them to restart the mill.
If the party arrives after dark, Maren is absent and Scene 2 begins with the gate already open.
The reed path left of the jetty leads toward the shrine.
A ledger page records a lock fitted to the sluice pin the week before the miller vanished.
If the party makes noise in the yard, Wick arrives from the wheel room within a few turns and the Scene 3 encounter begins on alert.
Tobiah Reed filed the sluice pin through from the inside so the wheel would jam and the mill would stop.
Wick and his wolfhound guard the sluice lever that frees the jammed gear.
Once the lever is pulled, the wheel turns and the cellar water starts to rise, leaving about five turns to finish the cellar.
If a character names Tobiah's debt or shows the filed pin, Wick lowers his cudgel and steps aside.
Wick yields if his hound is hurt.
Wick is owed three months of pay by Tobiah and will switch sides if he hears Tobiah never meant to pay him.
A side path offering a calm blessing and a hint toward the cellar.
The clay lamp gives a calm blessing: the next roll can be repeated once.
The shrine's keeper is long dead and Maren leaves the bread there in her father's memory.
If the party stays more than five turns, the water reaches the ceiling.
Staying too long means the party must leave without the miller or swim out at a cost.
Aldous carries a second copy of the sluice lock receipt.
If the party arrives with Wick as an ally, Aldous speaks freely.
Aldous hid in the cellar himself and Tobiah did not take him.
Maren wants the mill running again to pay her late mother's debt before the bailiff comes.
Tobiah wants the mill to fail so the bailiff will sell it cheaply to him.
Wick wants his unpaid wages and a safe road out of the valley.
The sluice pin sabotage is exposed and Tobiah Reed is named.
The bailiff cannot sell the mill, Maren keeps her home and the village eats.
The party leaves without exposing Tobiah, or the cellar floods with the miller inside.
The bailiff sells the mill to Tobiah and Maren leaves the bend for good.
